thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P0 alert — increased 503s from hosted inference cluster in us-west-2. Error rate jumped at ~12:41 UTC. Paging oncall. Logs: https://internal.logs/redwood/alerts/1990123456

lina_garcia: Ack. I'm oncall and taking lead. Starting triage now. Anyone seeing related deploys?

raj_patel: Not aware of any deploys on the infra side. I'm nearby to help with comms and paging.

morgan_lee: Support is already getting customer tickets citing timeouts — handful of high-priority customers affected. Estimated impact: some generation requests failing with 503s, intermittent latency spikes for others.

lina_garcia: Thanks @morgan_lee. First mitigation: rolling back last routing policy change to default traffic split, and disabling warm-up auto-batching to reduce pressure. Executing in 1 minute.

alex_chung: On it — starting rollback of routing rules on the canary fleet. Will monitor connection counts. If errors persist after rollback, we should fail open to lower-cost model variant (quantized) as fallback.

incident-bot: Deploy rollback job started by alex_chung (job 7682). Watch: https://ci.redwood/jobs/7682

emily_danvers: Drafting status page message below. Please review and make edits for phrasing. Will publish initial update once approved.

emily_danvers: ```
We are investigating increased 503 errors affecting text generation requests in the US-West region. Some customers may experience failures or timeouts. Our on-call team is actively troubleshooting and has initiated mitigation steps (rollback of recent routing changes and scaling adjustments). We will post updates approximately every 15-30 minutes or as significant progress occurs.
Impact: Some hosted API requests may return 503 or see increased latency.
Region: US-West (primary).
Root cause: Under investigation.
Next update: in ~15 minutes.
```

lina_garcia: Nice. Suggestions: change "rollback of recent routing changes" -> "rollback of a recent traffic routing policy" to be explicit. Also add: "no customer data was exposed."

raj_patel: Add an ask for customers: "If you see ongoing failures, please open a ticket and include request ids." keeps us actionable. Also drop the words "primary" after region to avoid overprecision.

morgan_lee: +1 on request ids. Also add a small line for enterprise CM: "We will proactively notify customers with confirmed impact."

emily_danvers: Updated draft with edits: ```
We are investigating increased 503 errors affecting text generation requests in the US-West region. Some customers may experience failures or timeouts. Our on-call team is actively troubleshooting and has initiated mitigation steps, including rollback of a recent traffic routing policy and temporary scaling adjustments. No customer data was exposed.
Impact: Some hosted API requests may return 503 or see increased latency. If you are seeing failures, please open a support ticket and include affected request ids.
Region: US-West.
Root cause: Under investigation.
Next update: in ~15-30 minutes or as progress occurs.
```

alex_chung: Looks good. From infra: after rollback we've seen a 40% drop in 503s in the canary pool. Rolling the rollback to remaining nodes now.

incident-bot: Update: rollback rollout at 30% — errors trending down in canary.

lina_garcia: Publishing initial status page update now. @raj_patel can you coordinate external support messages and customer CMs?

raj_patel: On it. I'll send an outbound note to active CMs and create a shared support doc with request id instructions.

morgan_lee: Support doc link: https://internal.docs/redwood/incidents/1990123456-support-note (adding affected customers list).

[15 minutes later]

incident-bot: Scheduled update reminder.

lina_garcia: Quick update: rollback completed to all nodes. Error rate down ~75% cluster-wide but still above baseline. Continuing telemetry and increasing pod counts by 20% to absorb load.

emily_danvers: Drafting second status update: ```
We have completed a rollback of a recent traffic routing policy and applied temporary scaling adjustments in the US-West region. Error rates have decreased by ~75% but remain elevated for some traffic. Our team is continuing to monitor and stabilize performance.
Impact: Intermittent 503s and elevated latency for a subset of requests.
Mitigation: rollback completed; temporary scale-up in place; ongoing monitoring.
Next update: in 30 minutes or when service is restored.
```

raj_patel: Good. For social channels, keep wording conservative: "service is degraded" not "partial outage" until we have clearer customer impact numbers.

alex_chung: Monitoring shows a small regression when burst traffic hits sequence lengths >1024 — suggests kv-cache pressure. If errors persist, plan B is to enable per-customer rate-limits for heavy requests.

lina_garcia: Noted. For now proceed with scale-up and add cache pressure metric to the incident timeline.

[~45 minutes after start] 

incident-bot: Metric alert cleared for 503 spike in us-west.

lina_garcia: Verified: 503s returned to baseline and latency normalized. I'll publish a resolved status page update. Thanks everyone for the fast turnaround.

emily_danvers: Drafting resolved notice: ```
Resolved: We have restored normal service in the US-West region. The team completed a rollback of a traffic routing policy and temporary scaling adjustments, and error rates have returned to baseline. We continue to monitor for regressions.
Impact: Some customers experienced intermittent 503s and higher latency during the incident window. If you continue to see issues, please open a support ticket and include request ids.
```

raj_patel: Sending proactive emails to impacted customers now. cc: support and CSMs.

morgan_lee: Logged post-incident checklist item: run load tests for long sequences (>1024) and add kv-cache pressure alert thresholds.

alex_chung: I'll open a follow-up RFC to harden routing policy rollbacks and improve canary sizing.

incident-bot: Incident 1990123456 marked resolved by lina_garcia. Duration: ~48 minutes. Resolution notes: rollback + scale adjustments. Links: status page, support doc, postmortem-queue.
